claims.statement: The kernel search state machine has one real state variable (`'idle' | 'active'`) plus a derived third UI state (`offline`) that the renderer paints: `activate()` moves idle to active, clears the query and is idempotent while already active; `deactivate()` is the single exit used for ESC, lost focus and a completed action and resets the generation, the debouncer, the rate-limit counter, the pending retry, the query, the last result set and the offline flag; and the service is born idle with `search/state` emitted only when the derived state actually changes.

`SearchService.setQuery` accepts text only while the machine is active and returns `false` in standby, and an empty string additionally clears `lastResults`, so a stray keystroke from a torn-down overlay can never reach the engine and an empty query leaves nothing for the action guard to match.

The kernel's `Debouncer` coalesces rapid typing to the last change inside a `DEFAULT_DEBOUNCE_MS = 200` ms window, suppresses re-sending a query equal to the last one it released (with a `1e-9` clock tolerance so float differences cannot stall a query), never fires on empty text, and exposes `feedDue`, which marks a query due immediately and clears the same-query record so an already-sent word can be re-sent.

Engine responses are single-flight-guarded by a generation counter that is incremented when a search starts, when the panel deactivates and when the kernel is disposed; every response is dropped when its captured generation is no longer current or when the machine has left the active state, so a late reply cannot overwrite newer results or resurrect results after ESC.

`classifyFailure` is the single failure decision point: a `ListaryNetworkError` or an `{"ok": false, "error": "SEARCH_UNAVAILABLE"}` payload becomes `offline`, `TOO_MANY_REQUESTS` becomes `rate_limited`, any other error payload or thrown value (for example a JSON parse error) becomes `error`, and any truthy `ok` payload yields `null`; the kind is decided before parsing, so an error payload can never be rendered as an empty-but-successful result set, and a reachable but misbehaving engine can never be classified as absent.

Both silent recoveries run through the pump: when a retry deadline passes while the machine is active, `SearchService.tick()` clears the deadline and calls `Debouncer.feedDue(this.query)`, so a retry re-sends whatever text is in the panel now (not necessarily the query that failed) through the same single-flight path, while a deadline that expires after deactivation does nothing because `tick()` early-returns unless the machine is active.

`SearchService.action(path, reveal)` refuses unless the exact path is a member of the most recent parsed result set — the kernel-side guard against arbitrary path execution, which closes automatically when the query is emptied — then either calls the injected `open` port (production `shell.openPath`, where a non-empty return string becomes the reported error) or the injected reveal port, whose production implementation spawns `explorer /select,<path>` with `stdio: 'ignore'` and swallows spawn failures, deliberately without `windowsHide` because that travels through STARTUPINFO as SW_HIDE and hides the Explorer folder window too.

Search coverage is layered rather than network-free: `app/tests/search/engine.spec.ts` pins the pure policy (debounce, request construction, response parsing, classification, backoff curve, loopback constants), `app/tests/search/client.spec.ts` runs the real client against a loopback fake API for refused connections, forced timeouts, non-JSON bodies and no-keep-alive, `app/tests/search/service.spec.ts` drives the machine and link with an injected clock and fake dependencies, `app/tests/contract.spec.ts` repeats the flow through the bridge plus two privacy guards, and the real-machine evidence is the acceptance battery's search section with `07-search-*.png` screenshots and the event log.

The search feature's ownership split is sharp: the cordis `SearchService` — backed by `app/src/main/search/engine.ts` for pure policy and `app/src/main/search/client.ts` for the only network I/O — owns the state machine, the debounce, the generation guard, the failure reactions and the execution of result actions, while the renderer only invokes `search/activate|query|deactivate|action` and paints the `search/state` and `search/results` events it receives.

`listarySearch` is a thin POST transport: the host is always the `BASE_HOST = '127.0.0.1'` constant imported from `engine.ts` and never taken from input or configuration, the port comes from `config.search.port`, the body is `buildRequest`'s `{ query, limit, offset }` JSON, and every request opens a fresh connection with `agent: false` and `Connection: close` because the API has no keep-alive.

The client draws the line `classifyFailure` relies on: a connection failure or the 3000 ms timeout (`HTTP_TIMEOUT_MS`, overridable per call) is wrapped in `ListaryNetworkError` — the only shape that classifies as `offline` — while an unparseable body rejects with a plain `Error`, which classifies as `error`, and the HTTP status code is never inspected, so the same non-200 answer delivered as JSON and as HTML lands in different kinds.

`parseResponse` is deliberately tolerant: a missing or non-object `data` degrades to `{ total: 0, items: [] }` instead of throwing, non-object rows are skipped, each row's `path`/`name`/`type` are stringified with `type` defaulting to `file` and `size_bytes`/`modified_at`/`score` defaulting to `0`/`''`/`0`, and no local truncation is applied — twelve rows are kept as twelve even though the service only ever requests `limit = DEFAULT_LIMIT = 8` at `offset = 0`, leaving paging and the display cap outside the search path.

`config.search.port` is the only search configuration: `defaultSearchConfig()` returns `{ port: BASE_PORT }` with `BASE_PORT = 38431` imported from `engine.ts` as the single source, `mergeSearch` accepts only an integer in `1..65535` and otherwise warns and falls back to the default, and pointing that port at a dead endpoint is the accepted way to reproduce the engine-offline path on a machine where Listary is running.

A 50 ms pump (`DEFAULT_SEARCH_INTERVAL_MS`) installed by `createKernel` and `createPanelKernel` calls `SearchService.tick()` and is the single decision point for debounce expiry, rate-limit backoff and offline retry; setting `searchIntervalMs: 0` disables the timer so offline tests can drive `tick()` from a synthetic clock, and `tick()` returns immediately unless the machine is active, so a standby panel never polls the engine.

Query text is memory-only and loopback-only: it lives in the service's `query` field, the debouncer's pending slot and the body of the local HTTP request, and the three search files are guarded by a behavioural test (a full search flow leaves no query text in the usage-log directory) and a source-level test forbidding usage-log references, `writeFileSync`/`appendFileSync` and hard-coded HTTP URLs in them.

The separate native search window documented by earlier revisions of this page is gone: ADR-0004 retired the Wallpaper Engine host and with it the ADR-0003 conclusion that the search panel had to be a service-owned Tk window, the search surface became an overlay inside the standalone panel, and the Tk window module and its tests, the dedicated acceptance scripts, the wallpaper spacer and the `/deck` panel-geometry handshake were deleted with it.

The service's reaction to a classified failure is three-way and only two branches recover silently: `offline` flips the derived state to `offline` (the inverted ENGINE OFFLINE badge) and re-arms a retry `OFFLINE_RETRY_MS = 3000` ms later, `rate_limited` leaves the display and the pushed state untouched and re-arms a retry after `backoffDelay(attempt) = min(500 · 2^(attempt−1), MAX_BACKOFF_MS = 5000)` ms, and `error` only logs and waits for the next input; an ok response clears the offline flag and the pending retry, resets the rate-limit counter, stores the parsed result set and emits `search/results`, while `deactivate()` also clears the offline flag so the badge cannot survive into the next activation.
